source: otp-v0.6 (2026-09-09): rubric-sp1.json (26 paragraphs, transcribed verbatim 2026-09-03) split at sentence boundaries into 32 single-sentence criteria per Igor's instruction; wording untouched. origins[i] = source paragraph number, or paragraph.sentence for a split paragraph.

levels.label: Beginner
paragraphs: Challenge provided to students is appropriate (not excessively difficult or excessively easy) for students to successfully engage in new learning.
One or more groups of students are not differentiated for and therefore make no progress.
The teacher is unresponsive to the needs of their students.
Student work observed does not provide evidence that is useful to determine progress over time.

levels.label: Emerging
paragraphs: Starting points may be established but response to these is variable with the data having no visible effect on the lesson structure, pace or progress.
One or more groups of students, (SEN, AMA etc), is ineffectively differentiated for and makes less progress than most students in the class.
A balance of pace is sought but doesn't effectively contribute to maintaining an effective pace of learning.
Collaboration and student student dialogue are a planned feature of the lesson but a lack of structure and/or poor timing reduces the effectiveness of the strategy.
Observations of student work do not provide enough evidence to confirm level of progress over time.

levels.label: Good
paragraphs: The teacher establishes clear starting points that lead to an explicit planned response.
Differentiated activities are provided to accommodate all groups of learners including any students with significant needs (SEN/AMA).
Lesson pace is well managed with planned strategies to support appropriate pace implemented.
Students are given structured opportunities to work together and do so with teacher guidance and support.
Tasks provided allows some students to access better than expected progress, (closed ended, low challenge, low cognitive load etc).
The teacher engages deliberately with groups to provide intervention and acceleration where appropriate.
Observations of students' work shows progress in line with curriculum expectations.

levels.label: Great
paragraphs: The teacher establishes clear starting points for students and adapts to their immediate needs, (grouping, support etc).
They provide and maintain challenge and pace for most groups of students, to ensure progress is not limited by learning that is too easy or too hard, with varied success.
In-lesson, unplanned interventions occur, and are mostly effective.
Students are provided with well structured opportunities to collaborate and engage in dialogue and these are mostly effective in terms of timing and/or implementation.
This allows more students to access better than expected progress.
Students can show and/or discuss their attainment and effectively share their new learning.
The teacher engages deliberately with groups to provide intervention and acceleration where appropriate.
Observations of students' work demonstrates a history of BtE progress over time from their individual starting point.

levels.label: Outstanding
paragraphs: The Teacher establishes clear starting points and responds to these to determine the best learning pathway for students, (more/less support, differentiated tasks, skipping unrequired learning etc).
They provide and maintain challenge for all groups of students to ensure progress is not limited by learning that is too easy or too hard.
Lesson pace is effectively maintained to provide a sense of urgency and enthusiasm for new learning.
The teacher is aware and responsive to the pace of learning for all groups of students.
The teacher engages deliberately with groups to provide highly effective intervention and acceleration where appropriate.

Most students participate successfully in tasks that promote effective collaboration and student student communication that provides them with opportunities to go beyond the limits of the activity and/or teacher expectations.
Students can accurately articulate and/or demonstrate the progress they have made in class in relation to their individual starting point for the lesson.
Observations of students' work supports a history of BtE progress over time and in lessons from their individual starting points.
